content: Emaho!Beyond the setting sun from here,Beyond countless many worlds,In a realm elevated slightly above,Lies the perfectly pure land of Sukhāvatī.Though my bubble-like eyes do not see him,He appears vividly in the clarity of my own mind.There dwells the Blessed Victor Amitābha,Blazing with the brilliance of a ruby’s hue.With a crown protrusion on his head and wheels on his feet,He is adorned with the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs.With one face and two hands, he holds an alms bowl in meditative equipoise,Wearing the three Dharma robes and seated in the cross-legged posture.Upon a seat of a thousand-petaled lotus and moon disc,Leaning his back against the tree of enlightenment,He gazes upon me from afar with eyes of compassion,To his right is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.His body is white, his left hand holding a white lotus.To his left is the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta,Holding a lotus in his left hand marked with a blue vajra,While his two right hands display the mudras of refuge and giving to me.The three main figures are like Mount Meru, the king of mountains,The retinue sits vividly, steadily, and resplendently,A hundred million monks who are Bodhisattvas,All golden in color, adorned with the major and minor marks.Clad in the three Dharma robes, they shimmer with a golden hue,Because in my devoted prostrations there is no distinction of near or far,I prostrate with devotion through my three doors of body, speech, and mind,To the Dharmakāya Amitābha, the Lord of the Family.From his right hand, light rays emanate as the emanation Avalokiteśvara,And further emanations of the Lord Avalokiteśvara, a hundred million.From his left hand, light rays emanate as the emanation Tārā,And further emanations of Tārā, a hundred million, are sent forth.From his heart-mind light rays emanate as the emanation Padmasambhava,And further emanations of Oḍḍiyāna, a hundred million, are sent forth.Homage to the Dharmakāya Amitābha!With the Buddha-eye, throughout the six periods of day and night,With compassion, you gaze forever upon all sentient beings.Whatever is thought within the minds of all sentient beings,Every stirring of conceptual thought, your heart-mind always knows.Whatever words are spoken by all sentient beings,You listen to them always, distinctly and without confusion.Homage to the all-knowing Amitābha!Except for those who have abandoned the Dharma or committed the acts of immediate retribution,All who have faith in you and offer prayers,Their aspiration for rebirth in Sukhāvatī is fulfilled,It is said you come in the bardo to lead them to that realm.Homage to the Guide Amitābha!Your lifespan endures for incalculable eons,You do not pass into nirvana, but remain here in manifest presence.If one prays to you with one-pointed devotion,Except for the ripening of past karma,Even those whose lifespan is exhausted will live for a hundred years;It is said that you avert all untimely death without exception.Homage to the Protector Amitāyus!More than offering gifts of the three-thousand-fold world systems,Filled entirely with precious jewels,Hearing the name of Amitābha and of Sukhāvatī,If one joins their palms with faith,It is said that this merit is greater than that;Therefore, I offer respectful homage to Amitābha.Whoever hears the name of Amitābha,And from the very depths of their heart and bones, without hypocrisy,Gives rise to faith even for a single moment,They shall not turn back from the path to enlightenment.Homage to the Protector Amitābha!Having heard the name of the Buddha Amitābha,Until the essence of enlightenment is attained,One will not be born as a woman and will be born into a noble lineage,And in all lifetimes, one’s ethical discipline will become perfectly pure.Homage to the Sugata Amitābha!My body, my possessions, and my roots of virtue,Whatever offerings are actually present,The mentally emanated auspicious substances, symbols, and seven precious jewels,The primordial trichiliocosm of the world,With its hundred million sets of four continents, Mount Meru, suns, and moons,And all the enjoyments of gods, nāgas, and humans—I take these in my mind and offer them to Amitābha.For my benefit, please accept these through the power of your compassion.Led by my parents, I and all beings,From beginningless time until the present,Have committed killing, taking what is not given, and sexual misconduct;I openly confess these three non-virtues of the body.Lying, divisive talk, harsh words, and idle gossip—I openly confess these four non-virtues of speech.Covetousness, ill will, and wrong view—I openly confess these three non-virtues of mind.Killing father, mother, teacher, or an arhat,And harboring ill will toward the body of the Victorious One—I openly confess having accumulated these five inexpiable deeds.Killing monks or novices, or causing a nun to break her vows,Destroying statues, stupas, or temples, and the like—I openly confess having committed these proximate inexpiable sins.Representations of the Three Jewels, temples, and the scriptures, and the like—Invoking them as witnesses, swearing oaths, and so forth,I openly confess having accumulated the negative karma of abandoning the Dharma.A sin greater than killing all sentient beings of the three realms—Slandering those who are Bodhisattvas—I openly confess having accumulated this great and pointless sin.The benefits of virtue and the drawbacks of non-virtue,The sufferings of the hells and their lifespans, and so forth—Even upon hearing these, I thought them untrue and mere conjecture;A negative karma more severe than the five inexpiable deeds,I openly confess having accumulated this inescapable negative karma.The four defeats and the thirteen remainders,The forfeitures, the individual confessions, and the five classes of misdeeds—I openly confess having violated the Pratimokṣa vows.The four black dharmas, the five and five and eight downfalls—I openly confess having impaired the Bodhisattva trainings.The fourteen root downfalls and the eight gross branch infractions—I openly confess having impaired the Secret Mantra samayas.Having committed non-virtuous acts without having taken vows,Such as unchaste conduct, drinking alcohol, and so forth—These are natural misdeeds, inherently blameworthy;I openly confess not having recognized these sins as sins.Although I have received refuge, vows, empowerments, and the like,I did not know how to guard their vows and commitments;I openly confess having incurred the downfalls of these prohibitions.Without regret, confession cannot purify;As if having swallowed poison, I view my past sins,And confess with great shame, fear, and remorse.Without the resolve to refrain from future misdeeds, there is no purification;Therefore, I vow from now on not to commit non-virtuous acts,Even should it cost my life, I hold this firm commitment in my heart.May the Sugata Amitābha and all his spiritual heirsGrant their blessings that my continuum may be completely purified.When I hear of others performing virtuous deeds,I abandon the non-virtuous mind of jealousy toward them,And with heartfelt joy, I rejoice in their actions;It is said that I shall obtain an equal share of their merit.Therefore, I rejoice in all the virtuesPerformed by noble ones and ordinary beings alike.Having generated the mind set upon supreme, unsurpassed enlightenment,I rejoice in all the vast activities performed for the benefit of beings.Abandoning the ten non-virtues constitutes the ten virtues;Saving the lives of others, practicing generosity,Maintaining vows, and speaking the truth,Reconciling those in discord, and speaking with gentle honesty,Speaking words of meaning, and having few desires,Meditating on love and compassion, and practicing the Dharma—In all these virtuous deeds, I rejoice.Throughout all the infinite worlds of the ten directions,For those who have not long since attained perfect Buddhahood,I beseech them to turn the vast wheel of DharmaWithout delay, for the sake of all beings;May your omniscient wisdom-mind perceive this request.Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and spiritual friends who uphold the teachings,To all those who intend to pass into parinirvāṇa,I pray that you do not pass away, but remain among us.By this, I dedicate all my virtues of the three timesFor the benefit of all sentient beings.May all swiftly attain unsurpassed enlightenment,And may the three realms of samsara be emptied from their depths.May the merit of this swiftly ripen within me,Pacifying the eighteen untimely deaths in this life.May I possess a healthy body, flourishing in youthful vigor,With inexhaustible wealth like the summer Gangā.Free from the harm of demons and enemies, may I practice the holy Dharma,And may all my dharmic aspirations be fulfilled as I wish.May I accomplish vast benefit for the teachings and for beings,And may I succeed in making this human life meaningful.May I and all those connected to me,Immediately upon passing from this life,See the emanated Buddha Amitābha,Surrounded by an assembly of monks,Appear directly before us.Upon seeing this, may my mind be joyful and my spirit light,And may I be free from the suffering of death.May the eight great Bodhisattvas,Through the power of their miracles, ascend into the sky,And may they show the way and lead meOn the path to Sukhāvatī.The suffering of the lower realms is unbearable,The happiness of gods and humans is impermanent,May a sense of fear toward these arise in my mind.From beginningless time until the present,In this cyclic existence, I have wandered for so long,May a sense of weariness toward it arise in my mind.Even if one is reborn as a human,One experiences countless births, old age, sickness, and death.In this degenerate age, obstacles are many.This happiness of gods and humans,Is like food mixed with poison;May I have not the slightest desire for it.Kinsmen, food, wealth, and companions,Are impermanent, like illusions and dreams;May I have not the slightest attachment to them.Lands, regions, and dwellings,Are like the houses in a dream;May I realize they are not truly established.From the inescapable ocean of cyclic existence,Just as one escapes from a great prison,To the pure realm of Sukhāvatī,May I go without ever looking back.Completely sever all ties of craving and attachment,Just as a vulture escapes from a snare;Across the sky in the western direction,Through countless world realms,Traversing them in a single instant,May I arrive in Sukhāvatī.There, having beheld the face of the Buddha Amitābha,Residing in direct presence,May all my obscurations be purified.Of the four modes of birth, may I attain the supreme,Within the heart of a lotus flower,May I take birth through miraculous transformation.In a single instant, may my body be perfected,And may I obtain a body endowed with the major and minor marks.Due to the doubt of fearing I might not be born,For a period of five hundred years,Within that place, though enjoying happiness and comfort,And even though I hear the Buddha’s speech,Because the flower has not yet opened,The fault of being late to behold the Buddha’s face—May such a thing not happen to me.May the flower open as soon as I am born,And may I behold the face of Amitābha.Through the power of merit and miraculous transformation,From the palms of my hands, may clouds of offerings,Inconceivable in nature, be emanated,And may I make offerings to the Buddha and his retinue.At that time, may that TathāgataExtend his right hand and place it upon my head,And may I receive the prophecy of my enlightenment.Having heard the profound and vast Dharma,May my mindstream be ripened and liberated.Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta,The two foremost Sons of the Victors,May you bless me and hold me in your care.Day after day, may I serve and honorThe countless Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions,As well as Amitābha,And when I travel to behold that realm,May I pay homage to them all,And receive the nectar of the Dharma.With unimpeded miraculous power,I shall go in the morning to the realm of Abhirati,The glorious realm,The realm of Las-rab-rdzogs, and the Ghanavyūha.To the Buddhas such as Akṣobhya, Ratnasambhava, Amoghasiddhi,And Vairocana,I shall request empowerments, blessings, and vows.Having made myriad offerings,May I arrive without hardshipAt the realm of Devacana by evening.Potala and Aḷakāvatī,Cāmara and the land of Oḍḍiyāna,A hundred billion realms of the Nirmaṇakāya,Avalokiteśvara and Tārā,A hundred billion Vajrapāṇis and Padmasambhavas.I shall meet them and make offerings with an ocean of offerings,And request profound empowerments and oral instructions.May I swiftly go to my own home, the realm of Great Bliss,And arrive there without any hindrance.My relatives, students, and others left behind,I shall see clearly with the divine eye.I shall grant them protection and blessings,And at the time of death, may I lead them to that realm.The duration of an eon in this Fortunate EonIs but a single day in Sukhāvatī.For countless eons, there is no death;May I always be established in that realm.From Maitreya up to the one who is aspired to,When the Buddhas of this Fortunate EonCome to this world,I shall arrive there through the power of miracles,Make offerings to the Buddhas, and listen to the sublime Dharma,Then, once again, to the realm of Great Bliss,May I go without any hindrance.May the hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas,And the arrays of qualities of all eighty-one buddha-fields,Gathered together as one,Surpass all other realms, supreme and unsurpassed;May I be reborn in that realm of Sukhāvatī.The precious ground is level as the palm of a hand,Vast, expansive, clear, and blazing with light.When pressed it yields, and when lifted it springs back;May I be born in that blissful, gentle, and vast realm.Wish-fulfilling trees are formed from many jewels,Adorned with silk leaves and fruits of precious gems.Upon them, flocks of emanated birds sing sweet melodies,Proclaiming the sounds of the profound and vast Dharma;May I be born in that realm of great wonder.There are many rivers of perfumed water possessing the eight qualities,And likewise, bathing pools of nectar,Surrounded by stairways and balustrades of the seven precious jewels.They are filled with fragrant lotus flowers and fruits,Radiating immeasurable rays of lotus-light;From the tips of these rays, emanated Buddhas are arrayed;May I be born in that realm of great marvels.The names of the eight states of no leisure and the lower realms are not heard,Nor the five poisons, the three poisons, sickness, or spirits,Nor enemies, poverty, conflict, and the like;The very sound of all suffering has never been heard in that realm;May I be born in that realm of great bliss.There are no women, and no birth from a womb;All are born from within the heart of a lotus.All possess bodies of golden hue, without distinction,Adorned with the crown protrusion and other major and minor marks.All possess the five clairvoyances and the five eyes;May I be born in that realm of immeasurable qualities.Celestial mansions arise spontaneously, made of various jewels;Enjoyments appear just as desired, simply by thinking of them.There is no need for effort or striving; all that is needed is spontaneously accomplished.There is no "I" or "you," and no grasping at a self.Clouds of offerings for whatever is desired arise from the palms of the hands;All are devoted to the unsurpassed Dharma of the Great Vehicle;May I be born in that realm where all happiness and joy arise.Fragrant breezes cause a great rain of flowers to fall;From all the trees, rivers, and lotuses,Pleasing forms, sounds, scents, tastes, and textures—Clouds of offerings and enjoyments arise eternally.Though there are no women, hosts of emanated goddessesConstantly make offerings with myriad offering goddesses.When I wish to sit, a precious celestial mansion appears;When I wish to lie down, a fine precious throne appears,With bedding of many silks, complete with pillows.Birds, fruit trees, rivers, and music and the like,When I wish to hear them, proclaim the melodious sound of Dharma;When I do not wish to hear them, no sound rings in my ears.Those pools of nectar and rivers, too,Become warm or cool, just as I desire.May I be born in that realm where all wishes are fulfilled.In that realm, the perfect Buddha AmitābhaRemains for countless eons without passing into nirvana;May I serve as his attendant for all that time.When, at some point, that Amitābha passes into peace,For a duration of eons as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,While the teachings still remain,May I never be separated from the regent Avalokiteśvara,And may I uphold the sacred Dharma for that entire duration.At the dusk and the dawn when the holy Dharma fades,When Avalokiteśvara has attained manifest buddhahood,As the King of the Mound of Glory, exalted by light in every direction,At the time when he is known by that name,May I serve him with offerings and listen to the holy Dharma.For sixty-six hundred thousand billion eons,During the time he remains,May I always serve and honor him,And uphold the sacred Dharma with the dhāraṇī of non-forgetfulness.After he passes into nirvana, for his teachings,Which will remain for six hundred and sixty million eons,May I uphold the Dharma during that time,And never be separated from the Mighty One.Then, when that Mighty One attains buddhahood,The Tathāgata of utmost stability,Who becomes the King of the Mound of Jewel-like Qualities,Whose lifespan and teachings are equal to Avalokiteśvara’s,May I always serve as an attendant to that Buddha,Making offerings and upholding all the sacred Dharma.Then, as soon as this life of mine has passed,In that realm or in another pure land,May I attain the state of a supreme, perfect Buddha.Once I am a perfect Buddha, like Amitāyus,May all beings be ripened and liberated merely by hearing my name,And through countless emanations guiding wandering beings,May I effortlessly and spontaneously accomplish immeasurable benefit for them.The Tathāgata’s lifespan, merit,Qualities, wisdom, and brilliance are immeasurable.The Dharmakāya is Amitābha, of boundless light,The Blessed One of immeasurable life and wisdom.Whoever holds your name,Except for the ripening of past karma,Will be protected from fire, water, poison, weapons,Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and all such dangers, as the Sage has said.I prostrate to you, holding your name,And pray that you protect me from all fears and sufferings.Grant your blessing for perfect and abundant auspiciousness.By the blessing of the Buddhas who have attained the three kāyas,By the blessing of the unchanging truth of reality,And by the blessing of the unwavering resolve of the Saṅgha,May these aspirations be accomplished just as they have been made.Homage to the Three Jewels.Tadyathā pañcendriyāvabodhanaye svāhā.The dhāraṇī for the fulfillment of aspirations.Homage to the Three Jewels.Namo Mañjuśrīye! Namo Suśrīye! Namo Uttamaśrīye svāhā!It is said that if one recites this and performs three prostrations, it becomes equivalent to one hundred thousand. From there, the supreme practice is one hundred, the middling is as many as one can, and the least is to perform at least seven prostrations. The supreme practice is to do this without interruption; the middling is to do so for a month or a year without interruption; and the least is to turn toward the west whenever one has the opportunity, visualize the realm of Sukhāvatī, join one’s palms toward Amitābha, and recite with one-pointed faith. By doing so, obstacles to one’s life in this world will be cleared, and there is no doubt that one will be reborn in Sukhāvatī in the next. This is the intention of the Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra, the Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra, and the Amṛtaprabha-nāma-dhāraṇī, among others. May this composition by the monk Rāga Asya become a cause for many sentient beings to be reborn in Sukhāvatī.
